draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Iritty! The town's icon is Iritty Bridge, built by the British about 100 years ago. Head east and you soon reach the Karnataka border.
draft.hungryLine: Iritty has lots of small restaurants, from homely rice porridge with fish fry to a cold kulukki sarbath by the bridge.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Start at Iritty Bridge, then drive out to Kottiyoor Temple, 33 km away, or Periya Forest on the Wayanad road.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Grab a kulukki sarbath at Iritty Bridge Cafe and watch the town go by.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Periya Forest has an orchid, Epipogium roseum, that lives for only one day.

spots.name: Kottiyoor Temple

spots.name: Periya Forest
spots.detail: 42 km away · 136 bird species and 109 kinds of butterfly

legends.title: The Vysakha festival
legends.body: Every year in June, Kottiyoor Temple holds its famous Vysakha festival. It's the big temple event of the area.

legends.title: The one-day orchid
legends.body: The forest is home to Epipogium roseum, an orchid that lives for only a single day. Lucky timing is the only way to see one.

tips.title: Plan for June at Kottiyoor.
tips.body: The Vysakha festival is held every year in June, so expect crowds then.

tips.title: Watch your step in Periya.
tips.body: Periya Forest is home to 11 species of poisonous snakes.

story.title: The British bridge
story.body: The British built Iritty Bridge, which became the symbol of the town. It still stands today.

story.title: Farming country
story.body: Nearby Aralam runs mainly on farming. Coconut, cashew, pepper, rubber and areca nut are the big crops.

story.title: The floods
story.body: Aralam was one of the worst hit areas in Kannur district during the 2018 Kerala floods.

story.title: A border town
story.body: Aralam, right next to Iritty, borders Karnataka to the east. Iritty is the stop for roads heading out to Kottiyoor and Wayanad.
